import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 244

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)
-/

namespace Erdos244

/-- Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_244 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ C > (1 : ℝ), 0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

/-- Romanoff [Ro34] proved that the answer is yes if $C$ is an integer.

[Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., _Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie_.
Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_244.variants.Romanoff {C : ℕ} (hC : 1 < C) :
    0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

end Erdos244

reformulations.difference: Lean includes k = 0, whereas Ding's explicit restatement of Problem 244 uses k ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The k ≥ 0 sumset is the k ≥ 1 sumset union {p + 1 | p prime}. The added set has counting function O(π(N)) = o(N), so the two lower densities agree for every C > 1. Ding explicitly notes this equivalence in §1. The set decomposition was proved in the scratch file; the density-zero argument was checked mathematically, not formalized.

reformulations.difference: The source's 'positive density' is expressed using positive lowerDensity, without requiring existence of a natural-density limit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Romanoff's footnote 1 defines positive density by N(x)/x exceeding a fixed positive constant for all sufficiently large x. For counting ratios, which lie in [0,1], this is equivalent to a positive liminf. The scratch file proves positive lowerDensity iff an eventual positive linear lower bound on the counting function. Strict versus non-strict bounds are interchangeable by decreasing the positive constant; endpoint conventions do not affect positivity.

sources_consulted: Yuchen Ding, On two Romanoff type problems of Erdős, arXiv:2503.22700v5, §1 and notation conventions; https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22700v5 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2503.22700v5

N. P. Romanoff, Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie, Math. Ann. 109 (1934), pp. 668–669, especially Satz II and footnote 1; https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gdzocr/PPN235181684_0109/00000672.xml and https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gdzocr/PPN235181684_0109/00000673.xml
review.notes:
No mathematical defects found in either declaration. Lean experiments confirmed natural-number exponents, the existential prime condition, ordinary-floor agreement for C > 1, identity of the floor in the integer-base variant, and bounded real-valued density ratios. Boundary checks included k = 0, C = 2, the excluded C = 1 case, and the minimum represented integer 3. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully, and the reviewed file was not modified.

Source-access limitation: the cited erdosproblems.com/244 page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The mathematical claims were verified instead against Romanoff's original paper and Ding's explicit restatement identifying this as Problem 244. Ding's latest version distinguishes the proved almost-everywhere result from the unresolved every-base question; the accessible Erdős metadata database also records 244 as open. No status mismatch was identified.
